correctness.rationale: The numerator g is strictly concave, positive at zero and tends to −∞. Its unique positive zero x_b has g′<0, hence H(x_b)<0; the displayed cutoff is the positive root of the multiplied quadratic. V′ has the sign of H and the positive factor (1+x)^3 turns H′ into Q with Q′<0. If Q(0)≤0 then H falls throughout; otherwise it rises to exactly one maximum at z and falls thereafter. Q(0)>0 implies b>c; x₀=√(b/c)−1 lies below x_b and H′(x₀)=(1+ηx₀)g″(x₀)<0, so z<x_b. The exact two-root test is then H(0)<0, Q(0)>0, H(z)>0; H(0)=0 is a boundary, not a first interior extremum. If H(z)=0, H′(z)=0 and H″(z)=Q′(z)/(1+z)^3<0: V′ is negative on both sides and V‴(z)<0, giving a stationary inflection. At or below η=2/(1−α), Q(0)<0 for all b,c>0. Above it choose b/c large enough for Q(0)>0 and first set a₀=(b−c)/(αη); then H(0)=0 and H(z)>0. A small positive perturbation of a makes H(0)<0 while preserving H(z)>0, proving realizability for each α,η above the frontier. Independent symbolic reconstruction of the stationary polynomial and exact signs at 0, 1/10 and 2 gives two roots below the buoyancy cutoff in the witness. The α=1/3 threshold is strictly η>3.
residual_risks: The frontier concerns existence over positive a,b,c, not all material choices above it; it does not apply where g≤0.
The physical use of creeping-flow spherical drag and the assigned load–mass–volume law is conditional, not an empirical conclusion.

originality.rationale: The exact result is for a specified rational excess-mass response and power-law volume drag, not general Stokes terminal velocity or the existence of competing physical effects. The checked alternate saturation models optimize different maps; the inspected physical model resolves different constitutive variables. No confirmed stronger theorem gives this family and two-root criterion. This is a best-of-knowledge judgment, with the closest motivating articles' unavailable passages explicitly retained as risks, not counted as exclusions.
residual_risks: The exact Yoshitake and Maggi model equations remain unresolved in independent retrieval, and Roberts full text could not be read. An exact earlier algebraic reduction in unavailable or unindexed literature cannot be ruled out.
The originality assessment is scoped to inspected evidence and does not certify historical priority.

value.rationale: Opposing buoyant loss, saturating mass gain and size-dependent drag motivate asking whether a load–speed curve can reverse slope twice before flotation. The work gives a strict universal exclusion/realizability boundary controlled by the ratio of the saturation and drag-load scales, and a usable necessary and sufficient coefficient test that includes the tangency. It is more informative than a numerical reentrant example or a slope calculation at zero. It provides a benchmark for evaluating this explicitly assumed response law; it does not make an ocean-wide prediction.
residual_risks: No data identify the coefficients, no evidence is given that natural aggregate trajectories attain the threshold, and the witness is not calibrated to turbulent, fractal or non-Stokes settling.
